claim: 150 EDTA blood dried blood spot specimens were tested, with AQUIOS CD4 counts spanning 5.0 to 1361 cells/uL and a median of 176 cells/uL
quote: ranged from 5.0 to 1361 cells/μL, with a median AQUIOS CD4 count of 176 cells/μL.

claim: The overall assay error rate was 4.6%, seven of 150 specimens, all from internal control failure, leaving 143 for comparison
quote: The overall assay error rate was 4.6% (7 of 150 specimens). All seven invalid/error results observed were due to internal control failure and were excluded from the final comparative analysis, leaving 143 DBS specimens available for method comparison analyses.

claim: Repeatability across triplicate PCR runs gave %CV values from 4.0% to 11.2%
quote: Strong repeatability was observed, with %CV values ranging from 4.0% to 11.2%.

claim: The highest imprecision was at the lowest CD4 count tested, 22 cells/uL, at 11.2% CV, while mid and high range values sat between 4% and 7%
quote: The highest variability was observed at very low CD4 counts (22 cells/μL; %CV, 11.2%), while mid- and highrange CD4 values showed improved repeatability, with %CVs predominantly between 4% and 7%.

claim: The concordance correlation coefficient between DBS i.Mune CD4 counts and AQUIOS flow cytometry was 0.91 with 95% CI 0.88 to 0.93
quote: yielding a concordance correlation coefficient (Pc) of 0.91 (95% confidence interval, 0.88-0.93)

claim: Bland-Altman analysis gave a mean bias of -28 cells/uL, or -6.9%, with limits of agreement from -267 to 209 cells/uL
quote: with the DBS specimens showing minimal systematic bias, with a mean bias of —28 cells/μL (—6.9%), and limits of agreement ranging from —267 to 209 cells/μL

claim: The outliers below the lower limit of agreement all came from samples with AQUIOS CD4 counts at or above 500 cells/uL
quote: A few outliers were identified below the lower limit of agreement, all corresponding to samples with AQUIOS CD4 counts ≥500 cells/μL.

claim: At the 200 cells/uL threshold, sensitivity was 93.8% and specificity 88.9%
quote: the i.Mune CD4 assay exhibited a sensitivity and specificity of 93.8% (88.4%-99.1%) and 88.9% (81.1%100.0%), respectively

claim: Percentage similarity analysis gave an average of 102.27% with a %CV of 26.36% against the standard of care
quote: The DBS i.Mune CD4 results exhibited an average percentage similarity of 102.27% with a %CV of 26.36% to the AQUIOS SOC, indicating minimal bias and consistent performance.

claim: Larger manual extraction batches were more variable: batch 1 with 28 specimens averaged 141.7% similarity with SD 96.75%, while batch 4 with 9 specimens averaged 98.24% with SD 8.97%
quote: with larger batches (eg, batch 1 with 28 specimens) exhibiting greater variability (mean percentage similarity, 141.7%; SD, 96.75%), whereas smaller batches (eg, batch 4 with 9 specimens) exhibited substantially lower variability (mean percentage similarity, 98.24%; SD, 8.97%)

claim: The authors concluded that processing smaller extraction batches may improve assay consistency
quote: These findings suggest that processing smaller extraction batches may improve assay consistency.

claim: Misclassification was worst in the 100 to 200 cells/uL band, at 31.0% overall, against 6.1% below 100 cells/uL
quote: Misclassification rates varied according to CD4 count range, with the highest variation observed in the 100 to 200 cells/μL category (Table 5).

claim: Below 100 cells/uL, all three misclassified samples were misclassified upward
quote: three samples were misclassified, corresponding to an overall misclassification rate of 6.1%. All misclassifications were upward.

claim: In the 100 to 200 cells/uL band, five samples were misclassified upward (17.2%) and four downward (13.8%)
quote: Of these, five samples were upwardly misclassified, corresponding to 17.2% (95% confidence interval, 7.6%-34.5%), whereas four samples were downwardly misclassified, corresponding to 13.8%

claim: Above 200 cells/uL, seven samples were misclassified, all downward, an 11.0% rate
quote: seven samples were downwardly misclassified, resulting in an overall misclassification rate of 11.0%

claim: The study is the first proof-of-concept assessment of an epigenetic qPCR CD4 assay on a dried blood matrix
quote: This study provides the first proof-of-concept assessment of an epigenetic qPCR-based CD4 assay applied to a dried blood matrix, DBS, a sample type routinely used in decentralized HIV programs.

claim: The observed sensitivity and bias meet WHO guidance for CD4 assay development, which asks for sensitivity above 90% and bias of 10%
quote: which recommends an acceptable sensitivity exceeding 90% and a bias of 10%

claim: Upward misclassification below 200 cells/uL risks leaving patients with advanced immunosuppression classified above treatment thresholds, delaying management
quote: upward misclassification among patients with true CD4 counts <200 cells/μL may result in patients with advanced immunosuppression being incorrectly classified above treatment thresholds

claim: Cobas plasma separation cards are proposed as future work, since the residual dried blood fraction discarded after viral load testing might support CD4 quantification from a single specimen
quote: Assessing whether this residual fraction can reliably support CD4 quantification could enable dual viral load and CD4 testing from a single specimen.

claim: Precision of the AQUIOS reference method was not assessed by replicate measurement, limiting direct comparison of analytical precision
quote: Precision of the AQUIOS CD4 reference method was not assessed through replicate measurements in this study, which limits direct comparison of analytical precision between the epigenetic assay and flow cytometry.

claim: All extractions were manual, which may have contributed to the batch-related variability and may not reflect an optimized or automated workflow
quote: All extractions were performed manually, which may have contributed to batch-related variability and may not reflect future optimized or automated workflows.

claim: Residual blood specimens vary in age, handling and storage history, which is a constraint on the performance observed
quote: The use of residual blood specimens is another constraint, as these samples can vary in age, handling, and storage history,
